newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian-U.S. crew redock with Mir after brief trip.
newsitem.headline: Russian-U.S. crew redock with Mir after brief trip.

text.p: Two Russian cosmonauts and a U.S. astronaut redocked with the Mir space station on Friday after a brief voyage around the station in their Soyuz escape capsule, Mission Control said.

Commander Anatoly Solovyov, engineer Pavel Vinogradov and British-born NASA physicist Michael Foale spent less than one hour outside Mir, during which they filmed the station ahead of risky repairs they must carry out on the crippled station.
"We've touched gently," Solovyov said in a radio link-up with Mission Control at Korolyov outside Moscow.
Mission Control officials said Solovyov had directed the Soyuz manually.

The Soyuz undocked on one side of Mir and redocked on the opposite side near the Spektr module which was damaged in a collision with a cargo ship on June 25, the most serious accident in Mir's 11 years in orbit.

Redocking the Soyuz near the Spektr means the cosmonauts will be able to make a quick escape if anything goes wrong during risky repairs to fix the damage done in the June accident. The repairs include sealing the Spektr.
